svg.text: Three-node Raft HA: restore database replicates to every peer via forceSnapshot

g.text: await the DB and the 30 users
await the DB and the 30 users
3 ArcadeDB containers on one Docker network, all given the same Raft server list.
All containers start in parallel; Testcontainers waits for each node's HTTP health probe.
Every node's cluster endpoint is polled once a second until one of them claims leadership.
GET /api/v1/cluster -> body contains "isLeader":true (the run fails after 60s)
Database and schema are written through the leader, which Raft carries to every follower.
CREATE VERTEX TYPE User, Photo - EDGE TYPE HasUploaded, FriendOf, Likes - UNIQUE_HASH / FULL_TEXT / GEOSPATIAL
30 users are written and converged, then SQL takes a backup on node 0, into that container.
The wrappers are closed, then the database is dropped everywhere - this is what the restore has to undo.
POST "drop database playwithpictures" -> 200, then until(!databaseExistsOnServer(0|1|2)) atMost 60s
The backup file lives only on node 0, and a restore from a follower cannot write a Raft entry.
The restore runs on node 0 and reaches the peers as a forced snapshot rather than as replayed transactions.
Two waits, in order: the database must be listed again on every node, then every node must count 30 users.
